presentation_title: Understanding AI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning
learning_objectives: Understand the core definition and goal of Artificial Intelligence.
Explain the concept of Machine Learning and differentiate it from traditional programming.
Identify real-world applications of Machine Learning.
Define Deep Learning and describe its relationship to Machine Learning.
Recognize practical examples of Deep Learning in action.
Compare and contrast Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning.
outline: At its core, Artificial Intelligence is a broad field of computer science focused on a simple goal: building smart machines capable of performing tasks that typically require human intelligence.
This could be anything from understanding language and recognizing images to solving complex problems.
The idea isn't new; it has been a dream of scientists since the 1950s, starting with pioneers who asked, "Can machines think?" AI is the entire universe of making computers intelligent.

Machine Learning is a type of AI. Instead of giving a computer a detailed list of rules to follow (traditional programming), we give it a lot of data and let it learn the rules for itself. It's all about recognizing patterns from examples.

Traditional Programming (Rules First): Imagine you want to program a computer to identify a cat. You'd have to write specific rules like: "IF it has pointy ears, AND it has whiskers, AND it has fur, AND it has four legs, THEN it is a cat." This is fragile
what if the cat's ears are folded?

Machine Learning (Data First): Instead, you show the computer thousands of pictures labeled "cat." The ML model analyzes all these images and learns the common patterns and features that define a cat on its own. It builds its own internal "rules" that are much more flexible and accurate.
Deep Learning is a super-powered, more advanced version of Machine Learning. It uses a structure called a neural network, which is inspired by the human brain.

These networks have many layers of "neurons" stacked on top of each other
and because there are many layers, we call it "deep."
This deep structure allows it to learn much more complex patterns from data than traditional ML.
Deep learning is the magic behind self-driving cars recognizing pedestrians, voice assistants understanding your commands, and the generative AI we'll discuss next.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and an interest in technology.

slides.title: Welcome to the Spoken Tutorial on AI, ML, and DL
slides.narration:
Hello and welcome to this **Spoken Tutorial**.
Here, we will learn about **Artificial Intelligence**, **Machine Learning**, and **Deep Learning**.
We will understand these important topics together.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
After this **tutorial**, you will know what **Artificial Intelligence** is.
You will also understand **Machine Learning** and how it is different from old ways of **programming**.
We will also learn about **Deep Learning** and its uses.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration:
To follow this **tutorial**, you need a **computer** with **internet**.
You also need a **web browser**.
You do not need to install any special **software** for this lesson.

slides.title: Prerequisites
slides.narration:
To do this **tutorial**, you should know how to use a **computer**.
You should also be interested in new **technology**.
You do not need to know **programming** or tough **maths**.

slides.title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
slides.narration:
**Artificial Intelligence**, or **AI**, is a big part of **computer science**.
Its main aim is to make smart **machines**.
These **machines** can do tasks that usually need human thinking.
Have you ever thought, 'Can **machines** think like us'?
slides.image_prompt: A futuristic robot thinking, with gears and light bulbs representing intelligence, set against a backdrop of computer science elements.

slides.title: AI: The Universe of Smart Machines
slides.narration:
**AI** can help **machines** understand language or see images.
It can also solve difficult problems.
This idea is not new; scientists have dreamt of it since the 1950s.
They asked, 'Can **machines** think?'
**AI** is the whole world of making **computers** smart.
slides.image_prompt: A timeline showing the evolution of AI, from 1950s concepts to modern applications, with icons representing different AI tasks like language processing and image recognition.

slides.title: Understanding Machine Learning
slides.narration:
Now, what is **Machine Learning**?
We call it **ML**.
**ML** is one part of **AI**.
Instead of telling the **computer** every rule, we give it a lot of **data**.
The **computer** then learns the rules on its own.
It finds patterns from many examples.
slides.image_prompt: A computer learning from a large dataset, with data flowing into a processing unit, and patterns emerging as a result of the learning process.

slides.title: Rules First vs. Data First
slides.narration:
Let us understand this with an example.
Imagine you want to teach a **computer** to find a cat.
In old **programming**, you write rules.
For example: 'If it has pointy ears and whiskers, then it is a cat.'
But what if the cat's ears are folded?
This method is not strong.
slides.image_prompt: A cartoon cat with distinct features, next to a flowchart showing rigid 'IF-THEN' rules for identification, highlighting the limitations of rule-based systems.

slides.title: Machine Learning: Learning from Examples
slides.narration:
**Machine Learning** works in another way.
You show the **computer** many pictures of cats.
The **computer** looks at all these pictures.
It learns what makes a cat a cat.
It makes its own rules that are much better and more correct.
slides.image_prompt: A collage of diverse cat images, with an arrow pointing to a machine learning model that is processing them and learning to identify a cat flexibly.

slides.title: Introducing Deep Learning
slides.narration:
Now, let us talk about **Deep Learning**.
**Deep Learning** is a very strong and advanced type of **Machine Learning**.
It uses something called a **neural network**.
This **network** works a little like the **human brain**.
slides.image_prompt: A stylized representation of a human brain next to a simplified neural network diagram, illustrating the conceptual inspiration for neural networks.

slides.title: The 'Deep' Structure
slides.narration:
These **networks** have many layers of '**neurons**'.
They are like many layers on top of each other.
Because of these many layers, we call it 'deep'.
This deep structure helps it learn very complex patterns from **data**.
It learns better than old **ML** methods.
slides.image_prompt: A multi-layered neural network diagram, emphasizing the many stacked layers of interconnected 'neurons' to represent depth.

slides.title: Deep Learning in Action
slides.narration:
**Deep Learning** helps self-driving cars see people on the road.
It helps voice assistants understand what you say.
It also helps with **generative AI**.
We will talk about this later.
See how **Deep Learning** makes our lives easier.
slides.image_prompt: A composite image showing a self-driving car detecting a pedestrian, a person interacting with a voice assistant, and a visual representation of generative AI creating art.

slides.title: AI, ML, DL: The Big Picture
slides.narration:
Let us quickly look again.
**AI** is the biggest field that wants to make **machines** smart like humans.
**Machine Learning** is a part of **AI** where **computers** learn from **data**.
**Deep Learning** is a special part of **Machine Learning**.
It uses many-layered **neural networks** for very difficult tasks.
slides.image_prompt: A Venn diagram showing AI as the largest encompassing circle, ML as a smaller circle inside AI, and DL as an even smaller circle nested inside ML.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
In this **tutorial**, you learned the main differences.
These are between **Artificial Intelligence**, **Machine Learning**, and **Deep Learning**.
We saw that **AI** wants to make smart **machines**.
**ML** helps **machines** learn from **data**.
And **DL** uses deep **neural networks** to find complex patterns.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Here is an assignment for you.
Think of one real-world use for **AI**, **ML**, and **DL** each.
Choose uses that we did not talk about in this **tutorial**.
Write them down.
Think about how each **technology** helps in that use.
